transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you. Well, I guess what pushed me to make this appointment is that I'm having a lot of trouble following through on things at work. 

I keep starting follow-up items after my audits, or after mentorship events, with every intention of finishing them. I really mean to. But then I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or a form just... never actually got done. It's happening a lot lately, and it's starting to affect my job, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
How much distress or anxiety do you feel about not being able to complete these tasks at work?

I don't know if I'd call it anxiety, exactly. I mean, I'm not panicking or anything like that. It's more just... really frustrating. 

It's stressful because I know I'm capable of doing the work, and I just look careless to my team when a simple review note doesn't get cleared. So, it definitely bothers me, but I wouldn't say I have actual anxiety about it. Just enough frustration that I knew I needed to figure out what's going wrong.
Do you find yourself easily distracted while working on these tasks?

Yes, very easily. If I'm trying to review an audit file, almost anything can pull me completely off track. It could be a Slack ping, someone talking outside my office, or even just... a random thought about my marathon training. Once my attention shifts, it's really hard to get back to the file I was working on.
Do you find your mind wandering or having trouble staying focused in situations outside of work as well?

Yeah, I do. But honestly, I notice it most whenever I have to sit through anything lengthy, even other things at work. 

Like, I can start a long client meeting or an AI-tool training and be fully engaged at first. But after a while... my mind just slips off. I'll suddenly realize I've missed the last few minutes of what was being said, even though I'm still sitting there looking right at the screen. It's like my brain just checks out without my permission.
Do you experience any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when you're in situations where you feel frustrated about not completing tasks?

No, I don't get anything like that. Like I mentioned earlier, it's not really a panic feeling for me. My heart doesn't race, and I don't get sweaty or shaky or anything. It's just... more of a mental annoyance with myself, rather than any kind of physical reaction.
Do you often feel guilty about things that happen in your daily life?

No, not really. I don't walk around feeling guilty about things in my daily life. I mean, I get frustrated when I can't finish an audit on time or when I zone out during a meeting, but it's not a deep sense of guilt. It's just irritation that I can't seem to stay on track.
Do you often worry about things in your daily life?

No, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I mean, I don't really sit around stressing about things that might happen. It's more just... dealing with the frustration of the things I actually mess up or forget in the moment, rather than worrying about everyday stuff in general.
Do you often feel like you're not good enough or that you're a failure?

No, I don't feel like a failure, and I don't really have those kinds of thoughts about not being good enough. Like I said, I definitely get annoyed with myself when I make careless mistakes at work or can't seem to just sit down and finish a task, but I know I'm capable. It's just... a struggle to get my brain to cooperate sometimes, not a feeling that I'm worthless or anything like that.
Have you had trouble with focusing or completing tasks like this in the past, before your current job?

Yes, it's actually been a lifelong thing. Even back in elementary school, my report cards always had comments saying I was bright but that I lost my assignments or rushed through things and missed small details. The teachers always noted that I talked out of turn and constantly needed reminders to finish my work. My mother still jokes about it—she says I could ace a test with no problem, but then I'd completely forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. So, yeah, this isn't new.
Do you have intense emotional reactions to situations, such as getting really angry or upset?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, like I mentioned, when I mess up or forget things. But I wouldn't say I have intense emotional reactions or get really angry or upset out of nowhere. It's just normal annoyance when I make a mistake, nothing extreme.
Do you have trouble organizing your time or tasks?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm an accountant, so I'm actually pretty used to structuring things. I know how to make a schedule and prioritize what needs to get done. The organizing part isn't really the issue for me. I haven't noticed any major problems with setting up my time or tasks... it's more just what I mentioned before, actually staying focused on the task once it's in front of me.
Have you ever acted on impulse, doing something without thinking it through?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really make rash decisions or jump into things without thinking them through. Being an accountant, I'm pretty analytical by nature, so I usually weigh my options before I act. I wouldn't say impulsivity is something I struggle with.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yes, actually, I do. When I'm sitting in meetings, I'm usually tapping my foot under the table, or clicking my pen. I end up shifting in my chair a lot, too. One of my colleagues actually joked recently that she can hear my leg going under the desk. So, yeah, I guess I do have a hard time just sitting completely still.
Were you restless or fidgety as a child?

Yeah, I was. It definitely showed up in class. Even back in elementary school, my report cards usually said I was bright, but... well, they always noted that I lost assignments, rushed past the small details, and talked out of turn a lot. The teachers said I constantly needed reminders to actually finish my work. 

My mother still jokes about it, actually. She says I could easily ace a test, but then I'd completely forget to hand in the project that was sitting right there in my backpack. So, yes, it's been there since I was young.
Did you have difficulty playing quietly as a child?

I don't really remember having an issue with that. I mean, I played like any other kid, I suppose. I don't recall my parents or teachers ever telling me I was too loud or that I couldn't play quietly. So, no, I don't think that was a problem for me.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're not at work or in a meeting?

Yes, it happens outside of work, too. But even just thinking about my job—like if I have to sit still for a long audit or review at home—it actually feels physically uncomfortable. It's like this... pressure starts building inside me. Eventually, I just have to stand up. I'll walk over to the printer, or just completely invent a reason to get up and move around because I can't take sitting there anymore.
